title: Ecosystem, maps, and integration hooks
summary: Glossary, sister systems, configuration, bridges from enterprise UC to the open projects, and the hooks those projects actually name.

lessons.title: Glossary and the mind map
lessons.summary: The glossary is a short definition plus a citation. The mind map is a topic picture, not a network diagram.
objectives: Read a glossary row as a pointer
Use the mind map to find a track
Refuse a definition that has no citation

sections.h: A glossary row is not the spec
paragraphs: Each glossary term in this lab is a short sentence and a citation. The citation is the authority. If you need the normative text, open the RFC or the vendor page named on the row. Quoting the glossary back as if it were the RFC is how a wrong timer gets into a design.

New rows for this edition point at RFC 7118, the open-source project pages, RFC 8224, the public laws, and The Campaign Registry. A row that says confirm has a label and no URL, because that link was not opened.

sections.h: The mind map is a table of contents
paragraphs: The ecosystem page draws a mind map with the markmap library already in this lab. The nodes are topics: signaling, media, the open core, compliance documents, and neighboring systems. A line in that drawing is not a trunk, not a VLAN, and not a failure domain.

Use it to choose the next track. WebRTC and SIP over WebSocket is the browser path. The open-source track is the four projects. The compliance track is the statutes and the identity RFCs, with the educational disclaimer. The rest of this track is how those pieces sit next to contact-center neighbors.

lessons.title: Sister technologies around the session
lessons.summary: WFM, recording, emergency policy, analytics, CRM, AI agents, and programmable APIs hang off the session. They are not SIP proxies.

Keep CRM and WFM out of the Via path

sections.h: What already has a protocol hook
paragraphs: Workforce management forecasts and schedules. A queue delay can surface as a SIP 480 or as carrier congestion, which is a SIP response, not a WFM object. Quality management scores calls. The standardized way to fork a session to a recorder is SIPREC, specified in RFC 7866 using SIP, SDP, and RTP.

Emergency calling is the neighbor with statutes, covered in the compliance track, plus RFC 6881 and RFC 6442. Analytics and CRM use data the contact center already has, such as the calling number. Amazon Connect's documentation, already used in this lab, describes attaching conversational analytics to an external voice system with a SIPREC connector. The CRM is not a SIP element.

The FreeSWITCH manual page says SignalWire's hosted platform includes AI agents behind REST APIs and SWML. That is a hosted product from the FreeSWITCH team, not a header in RFC 3261. A voice agent still needs a session, which on that page is the hosted engine.

Twilio's documentation home, opened for this edition, is titled as API reference, tutorials, and integration for Twilio products. This lab already uses Twilio's Elastic SIP Trunking documents for the SIP-shaped product. People call this class of product CPaaS. That word is not defined by an RFC this lab opened, so this page does not invent a protocol meaning for it. Read the vendor's current product page before you copy an architecture diagram that uses the word.

lessons.title: Configuration and troubleshooting seams
lessons.summary: Configure the file the project names. Troubleshoot the plane that failed. Do not copy a sample this lab did not print.
objectives: Point Asterisk SIP config at pjsip.conf and the dialplan at extensions.conf
Point a media-proxy problem at rtpengine's README
Separate a WebSocket handshake failure from a codec failure

illustration.title: Where to look
illustration.caption: Each row is a page this edition opened. Parameter names that are not on that page are not filled in.
rows: res_pjsip overview and the examples for your version
The users manual, which says it checked the source
SIP routing in front of the PBX
Kamailio home page, then the current module docs

paragraphs: Asterisk's PJSIP overview says the channel driver is chan_pjsip, configuration is pjsip.conf, and the dialplan is extensions.conf. The FreeSWITCH manual says SIP profiles and the dialplan, and it says its parameter tables were checked against the source. Kamailio's home page describes the SIP server role and tells you the project exists. Module parameters belong to the documentation set linked from that project, which this lesson does not copy.

rtpengine's README is the configuration authority for the media proxy: Linux, the Kamailio module, SDP rewriting, ICE, and SRTP bridges. A flag that is not in the README you opened is not in this lab. Synthetic sketches in the quizzes are labels, not files to install.

If the browser never sends SIP, stop at the WebSocket handshake and the sip subprotocol. If SIP completes and audio does not, stop at SDP, ICE candidates, and DTLS. If SIP completes, audio works, and the caller ID is the complaint, stop at the Identity header. If users cannot dial 911 without a prefix, stop at the statute and the FCC page, and do not place a live 911 call.
Write the observation beside the document. That is the whole method. A packet capture that you cannot tie to one of those documents is not yet a conclusion.

sections.h: What the existing lab already cites
paragraphs: CUCM is the enterprise registrar and the SIP trunk endpoint toward CUBE or another SBC. A CUCM SIP Profile is an administrative object. It is not a CUBE voice class sip-profiles list. UCCX call control goes through CUCM. Carrier SIP does not terminate on UCCX. CVP documentation describes SIP among the call server, gateways, and CUCM. Unity Connection's documented SIP integration sits on a CUCM SIP trunk. Those sentences are the bridge. This lesson does not add a menu click that the Cisco pages did not print.

Webex Calling premises PSTN uses a Local Gateway. Cloud Connected PSTN is a partner service, a different location setting. Teams Direct Routing uses a certified SBC and TLS to the pstnhub FQDNs. None of those vendor pages say to replace the SBC with an unstated open-source flag.

sections.h: The open side of the trunk
paragraphs: Kamailio's page says it can scale a PBX such as Asterisk or FreeSWITCH, and that it speaks SIP, including WebSocket for WebRTC. That is the open side. A SIP trunk from a Cisco SBC toward Kamailio or toward Asterisk is still SIP: Request-URI, Via, SDP, and the certificates the vendor requires. The open project's dialplan does not become a CUCM route pattern because both say SIP.

rtpengine stays on the media path when you need the proxy the README describes. It does not become a CUCM SIP trunk by itself. Draw the trunk, name the document on each side, and test emergency calling and identity with the compliance track's documents rather than assuming the trunk copied them.

lessons.title: Integration hooks that are already named
lessons.summary: Future work should use hooks the documents already name: AMI, AGI, ARI, the Event Socket, SIPREC, and SIP over WebSocket. This lab does not ship a live connector.
objectives: Name the control interfaces on the Asterisk license page

illustration.title: Hooks this edition can point at
illustration.caption: If a product advertises another API, open that page before you build to it. Empty cells stay empty.
rows: Not CRM screen pop by itself

paragraphs: The Asterisk license page names AMI, AGI, and ARI as management and control protocols. It states Digium's belief about GPL and applications that use those protocols. An integration that controls Asterisk can start by reading those interfaces in the documentation for your version. This lesson does not paste an ARI request.

The FreeSWITCH manual names the Event Socket and embedded scripting as the programming path for the server you run. The same page names REST and SWML for the hosted SignalWire platform. Pick the one that matches where the call actually runs. Kamailio and rtpengine expose their own module interfaces in their documentation. This lab stops at the roles their home pages and README state.

sections.h: Protocol hooks, and what is not built here
paragraphs: RFC 7866 is the hook for a recorder. RFC 7118 is the hook for a browser that speaks SIP. RFC 8224 is the hook for a signed identity. RFC 6442 is the hook for location in SIP. Those are specifications you can implement against. This repository does not run a registrar, a TURN server, or a campaign registry.

A webhook, a CRM connector, or a WFM feed that a vendor documents is real when you open that vendor page. It is not real because a mind map has a box labeled future. The ecosystem page lists the neighbors. The next integration should name the document, the message, and the test. Until that page is opened, the sources block says confirm and prints no URL.
